description:
Krakow Jagiellonian University, the first higher education institution to provide education in Poland and the second educational institution with higher education status opened in Europe, is one of the oldest universities in the world. The Jagiellonian University, which has been operating for about 650 years, has become one of the symbols of the city of Krakow over time.

Almost every faculty of the university is shown as the number 1 in Poland in their branches. Today, the Jagiellonian University has nearly 46,000 students, 3,700 academic staff, and about 500 distinguished professors.

Jagiellonian University, the oldest and most established university in Poland, is also one of the oldest educational institutions in Europe. It was founded on 12 May 1364 by King Casimir of Poland. Since its first establishment, it has always been an international institute and has attracted students from all European countries in ancient times. The most important historical figures who studied at this University are Nikolas Copernicus and Pope Jon Paul II.

Ranked 307 in the World Rankings, the university has a historic campus in Krakow City center and a new modern campus. Jagiellonian University, which tests various specialization opportunities in the humanities and social departments and has the best Medical Faculty in Poland, offers master's and double degree programs. The Modern Research Center also provides dormitories within the university campus, which provides various opportunities to students in terms of university life with international student unions. The dormitory prices of the university start from approximately 100 Euros.

Jagiellonian University, which contributes to the fascinating historical spirit of the city with its historic campus in the very center of Krakow, celebrated its 650th anniversary in 2014.
